trust_decision.summary: UploadServlet.getUploadDir(HttpServletRequest) decides where (and whether) a multipart upload from a /upload caller is staged on disk; at the pinned commit a caller without an open LogicalDOC session falls back to a freshly created HttpSession folder, and /upload is permitAll, so anonymous callers can stage files.

landing_point.why: The advisory names UploadServlet; doPost is the only handler and where the upload is parsed and written.

fix_sites.module_kind: servlet handler helper (same file as the landing point); fix.diff:397-405 replaces getSession(true) fallback with getSession(false) or throw

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other multipart-to-disk route, /uploadresource, validates the LogicalDOC session before parsing (DocumentResourceUpload.java:82), so a solver can correctly say it is not an unauthenticated route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Authenticated GUI uploads to /upload keyed by the LogicalDOC sid must keep working, because they feed GWT services that consume UploadServlet.getUploads(sid) (documents, contacts, attribute sets, security). A fix that rejects every caller without an HttpSession, or one that requires Spring authentication on /upload, risks breaking that flow.

O6_input_shapes: request with no sid and no HttpSession (anonymous)
request with a sid that is unknown or closed (falls to the same else branch at UploadServlet.java:127)

O7_producer.where: logicaldoc-webapp/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/web/UploadServlet.java:224-236 (getSid calls request.getSession(true) at :230 when no servlet session is bound to the sid, including sid == null via SessionManager.java:667-669)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getUploads(HttpServletRequest) keeps its own getSession(true) fallback, so it can create an anonymous session-backed upload map independently of getUploadDir.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a copy of the getUploadDir dispatch logic. A maintainer patching one helper could easily leave the twin unchanged.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getSid creates the HttpSession (line 230) before getUploadDir checks it, so a check based on 'session exists' is satisfied by the servlet's own side effect (a how-type ordering sibling).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This exists in the real code: getUploadDir(request) calls getSid first (line 123). The published check at fix.diff:397 appears to inherit this ordering.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second multipart parser with no setFileSizeMax/setSizeMax; a planted variant reached before session validation would be a real second implementation at distance (util package).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ServletUtil already holds a separate ServletFileUpload setup used by DocumentResourceUpload; adding another permitAll servlet that calls it is plausible.

O9_family: CWE-770 unauthenticated resource allocation (disk fill via anonymous upload staging); authorization gap on a permitAll servlet

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module (Java 17+/jakarta servlet, Spring Security, GWT front end)
O10_build.project_tests: No UploadServlet test exists at the pinned commit; webapp service tests (e.g. logicaldoc-webapp/src/test/java/com/logicaldoc/web/service/DocumentServiceImplTest.java) use UploadServlet.getUploads; MockServletRequest exists in logicaldoc-util/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/util/servlet/MockServletRequest.java

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace getSession(true) with getSession(false) in getUploadDir and reject when null. This is the published fix, and it looks defeated by getSid creating the session first.

out_of_scope_notes: /uploadresource (DocumentResourceUpload -> ServletUtil.uploadDocumentResource, ServletUtil.java:730-736) parses multipart with no size limit, but only after session validation; this is an authenticated resource issue, not this advisory's property.

The published fix looks ineffective at its own site: getUploadDir(request) calls getSid (UploadServlet.java:123), which calls request.getSession(true) (UploadServlet.java:230) whenever no servlet session is bound to the sid, so getSession(false) at fix.diff:397 would be non-null for anonymous callers. This is worth confirming against the upstream follow-up.
